statement: You receive a positive integer n. Decide whether n is a power of two, meaning its binary row holds exactly one set bit. Use the erase identity: n AND n-1 removes the lowest set bit, so the result is zero exactly when that bit was the only one. Print 1 for a power of two and 0 otherwise.
constraints: The input is a single integer on one line.

example.why: 64 is 1000000; erasing its only set bit leaves zero, which certifies the power of two.

hint: One subtract, one AND, one comparison with zero - resist the urge to loop.
mistake: Dividing by two in a loop and declaring odd intermediate values failures - correct but slow, and easy to get off by one.
